title: After hours at Maddox's: Monk and Dizzy; "Bebop" a misnomer
summary: He heard Monk and Dizzy play after hours at a 137th Street bar, uttering "bebop" sounds, and thinks the name a misnomer.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Now, going back to Monk's time, I remember to the wee hours of the morning, a place called... Mack Maddox had a place, another one of the early hours(?) bars...
Maddox, at 137th Street. Musicians would go to these places after work, you know, and just play somewhere until the wee hours. I'd see Dizzy and hear Monk

playing into the wee hours of the morning, and they'd be uttering these guttural sounds -- "IDDIX-BA, BAT-DA, BAT-DA, BEBOP." [LAUGHS] But I never paid any attention to them, really. To me that was...
Yeah, both Monk and Dizzy would be playing. Way after hours; you know, you can't play loud.

Actually, to me that's a misnomer. Those were sounds that in the act of playing you automatically utter, I suppose. But harmonically and musically, it's very sound. I mean, the figurations that they were playing and the interpretation was a good interpretation, you know. It was very sound music. And I think that putting the name of Bebop I guess maybe appealed to the public. I don't know how it came out. I mean, to me it's like a misnomer. I think it should have a more dignified name, but it is good playing harmonically.
